automation.heroLabel: AI for construction and civil engineering · Zurich area
automation.metaTitle: AI for construction and SMEs near Zurich | Dominic Furchert
automation.heroTitlePre: Three things AI can do in construction
automation.heroSub: I'm Dominic Furchert. I set up ready-made AI tools in construction and civil engineering firms with 10 to 50 people east of Zurich, show them to your people and measure after 6 weeks whether they are used. At a fixed price.
automation.metaDescription: Site reports by voice, quote drafts from enquiries: Dominic Furchert sets up AI tools in construction firms near Zurich. Free live demo.
automation.heroTilesNote: Examples with invented names. Everything runs on your own licences, not on my systems.
automation.heroCtaMicro: 30 min · free · at your firm or by video
automation.heroCallback: Prefer the phone? Request a call back →
automation.workHeading: You know your firm. I know the tools.
automation.workLead: The tools already exist: they turn a voice message into a draft report, find similar quotes and summarise tenders. I set them up at your firm and show them to your people, on site and in the office.
automation.workRight1: You check and approve whatever is sent or signed
automation.workRight2: You do the pricing as always
automation.workRight3: You decide how to run your sites
automation.workFootnote: Examples of tools: Microsoft 365 Copilot for e-mail and files, and a site-report app such as Benetics. I don't sell licences.
automation.exampleHeading: How a voice message becomes a time-and-materials report
automation.exampleLead: After the extra work, the site foreman speaks into his phone for two minutes and attaches three photos. The report app turns this into a draft. Marked items are checked before it is sent.
automation.processHeading: What does it cost, and how does it work?
automation.processLead: Four steps. You have the price of each step in writing before it starts. After each step, you decide whether to go on.
automation.priceFootnote: Fixed prices in Swiss francs. “People” means everyone at the firm, on site and in the office together. You pay for licences yourself, directly to the vendor or through your IT partner; they belong to you.
automation.privacyLead: The licences are in your firm's name. Your data sits in your own accounts with Microsoft and the app vendor, not on my servers. What we watch for: site photos in private chats, folders open to everyone, and unclear data routes.
automation.privacyRight1: Copilot only shows each person what they can already open today. So we first check who can access payroll and HR folders. It is about permissions, not content.
automation.privacyRight2: I work with my own account in your Microsoft 365, with only the rights needed. You can block it at any time.
automation.privacyRight3: Before the start you get a data sheet: which tool processes which data where, with all exceptions.
automation.privacyFootnote: According to Microsoft, Copilot processes prompts within the EU Data Boundary, which includes Switzerland, and does not use them for training. Exception: if web search is switched on, the boundary does not apply to the search queries sent to Bing. Microsoft does not commit to processing in Switzerland only. I do not give legal advice.
automation.aboutMiniText: I work in the Zurich area. I did my apprenticeship as an application developer (EFZ) at UBS and an IT audit internship at KPMG. Today I study computer science at the University of Zurich. As president I lead a rowing club with about 200 members, including a multi-million-franc infrastructure project and a national regatta. I use AI myself: an assistant may read my email and calendar, and I built the connection. I built a second one for the rowing club. I come to you, to your firm and to your sites.
automation.reliableTitle: You can rely on me. In practice that means:
automation.reliable1: A reply by the next working day at the latest
automation.reliable2: A fixed price in writing before anything starts
automation.reliable4: I keep appointments. If something comes up, I let you know beforehand.
automation.bottomCtaHeading: In 30 minutes you see what would work at your firm.
automation.bottomCtaSub: You tell me what takes up your time. I show you what works today. If it won't help you, I'll tell you.
automation.bottomCtaAgenda: How the half hour goes: for 10 minutes you tell me where things get stuck. For 15 minutes I show you what works today, with sample data; if you like, you speak a Regie report into the phone yourself. In the last 5 minutes you tell me whether you want more. You don't need to prepare anything.

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.gatesub: This area is reserved for the homelab operator. Sign in via furchert.ch to continue.

services.title: Services
services.subtitle: CPU and memory per workload (highest container, share of its limit), daily availability and container restarts for the apps and homeassistant namespaces. Data from Prometheus, loaded fresh on every page view; history is limited to its 14-day retention.
services.partial: Some data could not be loaded: {groups}. Affected values show —.
services.restartsUnknownColours: Restarts are unknown for some or all services; their colours reflect availability only.

legend.title: Legend
legend.todayHint: Rightmost bar = today; click it for the last 24 h

services.usageNone: No usage data, or no limit and no request set
services.toggleLabel: Hourly view of the last 24 h for {name}

network.title: Network
network.subtitle: Inbound traffic through Cloudflare, source-IP reputation, firewall events, LAN access to the cluster nodes, egress from cluster workloads and form logins at auth-service. Data from data-service, loaded fresh on every page view.
network.disabled: data-service not configured in this environment (DATA_SERVICE_URL unset).
network.malformed: Unexpected response from data-service — no data shown.

status.title: Collectors
status.failures: {count, plural, one {# consecutive failure} other {# consecutive failures}}

warningHint.upstream: The last run succeeded but its source has no data yet.
warningHint.truncated: The last run succeeded but hit a size limit; some rows were dropped.
warningHint.partial: The last run succeeded but skipped malformed source rows; the rest was stored.
warningHint.generic: The last run succeeded with warning {code}.

ip.title: IP detail
ip.notFound: This IP was not seen in the window.

lan.title: LAN (cluster nodes)
lan.subtitle: Connections, firewall blocks and SSH logins at the four cluster nodes, from each node's conntrack table and journal.
lan.connectionsNote: Peak concurrent TCP connections per 15-minute window, by source and conntrack state.
lan.ufwNote: UFW rate-limits its log, so these counts are a lower bound.
lan.fromListedRows: {count, plural, one {Derived from the # listed row.} other {Derived from the # listed rows.}}
lan.sshNote: Failed counts failed authentication for existing users and is a lower bound: sshd logs rejected keys only when a connection gives up. Unknown usernames count as invalid user. SSH through the Cloudflare tunnel shows up as a pod or node address, not the real client.
lan.noDataYet: No LAN data yet: the node collector has not reported. Data appears about 30 minutes after the netmon_node role is rolled out to the nodes.

egress.title: Egress
egress.subtitle: Outbound TCP connections from cluster workloads to external destinations, from the coroot node agent's per-container counters. Hourly aggregates; FQDNs come from DNS answers the agent observed.
egress.newHint: Not seen for this workload and destination in the previous 30 days.
egress.fromListedRows: {count, plural, one {Totals derived from the # listed flow (top flows by traffic).} other {Totals derived from the # listed flows (top flows by traffic).}}
egress.note: A destination's first hour can be undercounted: the counters only start when the agent first sees the connection.
egress.noDataYet: No egress data yet: the egress collector has not succeeded. Data appears about an hour after the coroot node agent runs on the nodes.
egress.emptyHint: If this stays empty, check that the coroot node agent runs on the nodes.
egress.disabledHint: The egress collector is disabled in data-service.

logins.title: Logins
logins.subtitle: Form-login attempts at auth.furchert.ch, pulled from auth-service's login-event outbox. Attempted usernames are never stored; failed attempts are linked to known accounts only through a keyed hash.
logins.listedNote: IP and account counts come from the listed rows (top 50 each); the outcome totals cover the whole window.
logins.byIp: Top source IPs by failed and locked attempts
logins.bySubjectNote: Failed counts only failures whose username hash matches one of the account's successful logins; locked attempts are not included. Rotating auth-service's login-event hash key breaks this link for older events.
logins.usernameTagHint: First 8 characters of the keyed username hash: equal tags mean the same attempted username. The username itself is never shown.
logins.eventsNote: Newest first. The IP source says whether the address came from Cloudflare's CF-Connecting-IP header or the TCP peer; both can be spoofed inside the cluster.
logins.noDataYet: No login data yet: the login-events collector has no source data (auth-service's login-event outbox is not enabled yet, or the collector has not run).
logins.failingHint: The login-events collector is failing, so logins in this window may be missing; see the collector status above.
logins.invalidPage: This page of login events is no longer valid.
logins.disabledHint: The login-events collector is disabled in data-service.
logins.credentialsHint: The login-events collector cannot authenticate at auth-service: set AUTH_CLIENT_SECRET for data-service (Secret data-service-secrets, key auth-client-secret) to the secret of auth-service's data-service client, then restart the data-service pod.

noAccess.title: No access
noAccess.body: You are signed in, but this page is reserved for accounts with the ADMIN role.

reauth.title: Sign in again
reauth.body: Your session has no valid access token for the auth-service admin API (it predates this console or has expired). Sign in again to continue.

states.disabled: auth-service is not configured in this environment (AUTH_SERVICE_URL unset).
states.unauthorized: auth-service rejected the access token — sign in again.
states.forbidden: auth-service denied access: your token lacks the ADMIN role.
states.not_found: Not available yet — this auth-service version does not serve the endpoint.
states.unexpected: Unexpected response from auth-service — nothing is shown rather than guessing.

overview.recentActivityBody: auth-service has no audit API. Login events are shown on the Network page.

users.pageOnlyFilter: Search and filters apply to this page only.

drawer.passwordHint: 8–72 characters · stored as a bcrypt hash; never returned via API.
drawer.resetHint: POST /api/v1/users/{id}/reset-password — admin path, no current password required. Ends the user's sessions.
drawer.resetDone: Password updated. The user's sessions were revoked.
drawer.confirmDelete: Delete user {username}? This also revokes their sessions.
drawer.inactiveHint: INACTIVE revokes the user's sessions and consents immediately.
drawer.selfHint: This is your account — renaming, deleting, deactivating or demoting it is disabled.

clients.ssoNote: SSO/OIDC clients (grafana, n8n, open-webui, …) are defined in auth-service's application.yaml and cannot be managed here.
clients.clientIdHint: [a-z0-9-], 3–32 characters — also the device's MQTT username.
clients.confirmRevoke: Revoke device client {clientId}? New tokens fail immediately; issued tokens stay valid until they expire (≤ 1 h).
clients.secretBody: Shown exactly once — auth-service only stores a bcrypt hash. Copy it into the device configuration now.

jwks.rotationBody: auth-service has no rotation API — keys come from a Kubernetes Secret. Rotating invalidates every issued token immediately (INTERFACES.md, Important Notes #4).

unavailable.sessionsBody: auth-service exposes no API to list or revoke OAuth2 authorizations. Deactivating, deleting or resetting a user's password revokes their sessions.
unavailable.auditBody: auth-service exposes no audit API. Login events (success, failure, locked) are collected by data-service and shown on the Network page.

errors.session: Your session expired — sign in again.
errors.self: You cannot rename, delete, deactivate or demote your own account.
errors.notFound: Not found — it may have been deleted meanwhile.

reauth.title: Sign in again
reauth.body: Your session has no valid access token for device-service (it has expired or predates this console). Sign in again. If this message comes back afterwards, device-service is rejecting furchert.ch tokens — that is a token configuration problem, not your session.

states.disabled: device-service is not configured in this environment (DEVICE_SERVICE_URL is missing).
states.unavailable: device-service is unreachable — please try again in a moment.
states.unauthorized: device-service rejected the access token — please sign in again.
states.forbidden: device-service denies access: your token lacks the ADMIN role.
states.not_found: Not found — this device-service version does not offer the endpoint.
states.unexpected: Unexpected response from device-service — showing nothing instead of guessing.

overview.sub: device.furchert.ch · port 8081 · K3s/apps · schedules in UTC
overview.noLiveBody: The last message came on {when} from {device}. The values shown are the last reported ones and control is locked. device-service still sends active schedules — nobody receives them.
overview.noLiveBodyNever: No device has ever reported. Control is locked.
overview.upcomingNone: No active schedule has a next run.

devices.later: Registering and deleting devices comes in a later version of this page.
devices.none: device-service knows no devices yet. A device appears here after its first MQTT message.
devices.lockedOffline: Control locked: {device} is offline. Commands are not stored and would be lost.
devices.lockedStale: Control locked: the last message from {device} came {rel}. Commands are not stored and would be lost.
devices.sent: {field} → {state} sent to {device}. The state shown changes only once {device} reports it.

schedules.fanout: A schedule applies to every terrarium: device-service sends it to terraGeneral/‹function›/schedule, which every terrarium receives. The device is only a grouping label.
schedules.twoSchedules: A schedule sets one state. "On in the morning, off in the evening" takes two schedules.
schedules.none: No schedules yet. Create the first one with "+ New schedule".
schedules.savedActive: Schedule #{id} saved. Next run according to device-service: {abs} ({rel}).
schedules.savedInactive: Schedule #{id} saved — inactive, it does not run.
schedules.savedNoRun: Schedule #{id} saved. device-service cannot work out a next run for this expression.

cron.customHint: Spring cron with 6 fields, seconds first, in UTC — or a macro such as @daily. Example: 0 30 6 * * MON-FRI = Monday to Friday 06:30 UTC. device-service shows the next run after saving.
cron.dailyMeans: Runs daily at {local} Zurich time ({utc} UTC).
cron.dailyShift: From {date} it runs at {shifted}, because device-service works in UTC. To keep {intended}: after the switch, open the schedule, set {intended} again and save.
cron.intervalMeans: Runs every {minutes} minutes, counted from the full hour.

drawer.deviceHint: Grouping only — the schedule reaches every terrarium.
drawer.deviceFallbackHint: Device list unavailable — type the name ([a-z0-9-], 3–32 characters).
drawer.legacyPayload: The stored payload {payload} is not in the standard format. Saving replaces it with the chosen target state.
drawer.confirmDelete: Delete schedule #{id}? It will not run any more.

errors.session: Your session has expired — please sign in again.
errors.payload: This schedule has no standard payload; activating or deactivating it would overwrite it. Open "edit" to change it.
errors.notFound: Not found — it may have been deleted meanwhile. Reload the page.
errors.unavailable: device-service is unreachable or failed — nothing was confirmed. Check the state and try again.

fields.field: Choose light, night light or rain.
fields.state: Choose switch on or switch off.
fields.cronFields: Spring cron needs exactly 6 fields, seconds first (e.g. 0 0 7 * * *), or a macro such as @daily.
fields.cronSeconds: The seconds field must be a single number (0–59). Otherwise the schedule would switch every terrarium several times a minute.
